comparison_design.note: head_to_head=true means the fixed opponent is the baseline AI, so the candidate seat meets it directly and the baseline arm is a mirror control. head_to_head=false is a common-opponent benchmark: both arms face the same fixed field and never each other. The two designs answer different questions and are not pooled.

saturation.note: ceiling_limited=true means the stronger arm already takes at least threshold_pct of first-place credit in this condition, so a +5 pp difference cannot be resolved here. Change the opponent field or the mode rather than reporting a small delta as a strength difference.

throughput_note: games_per_second and decisions_per_second use the summed per-game wall time of this shard set as the CPU denominator. They are single-process throughput measurements, not parallel speedup or latency.
measurement_scope: focus-seat whole decision: action-space selection plus detail generation; rates use focus-only decisions as denominator
whole_decision_budget_note: whole_decision_budget_enforced=true means the reported budget bounds selection and detail generation together: the search deadline is the budget minus detail_reserve_ms. observed_all_decisions_within_* are measurements of the recorded decisions, not an OS real-time guarantee, and they are false in simulation-capped mode because no clock applied.
candidate_10s_observed_pass_basis: whole-decision budget (selection + details) enforced for the focus seat, a positive budget <= 10000 ms, and the measured maximum focus decision within budget + tolerance
timeout_rate_semantics: timed_out means the wall-clock deadline ended that decision. In time-budgeted mode that is the normal case and therefore close to 1.0; in simulation-capped mode no deadline is applied, so the rate must be 0.0.
search_mode_note: simulation-capped and time-budgeted are different experiments and must not be pooled: the first caps the number of simulation attempts and is reproducible, the second fixes wall-clock cost and is not. deterministic_policy_selection is true only when no deadline was enforced for the focus seat.
caveat: First-place credit values are probability fractions (0.05 = 5 percentage points); *_pp fields are percentage points. Focus decision timing includes action-space selection plus detail generation for the arm ordered as candidate/baseline. *_10s_observed_pass is an observed check, not an OS-enforced hard guarantee. It is true only when the whole-decision budget was enforced for the focus seat (time-budgeted mode; selection *and* detail generation under one clock, whatever the focus policy), a positive budget <= 10000 ms was applied, and the measured maximum focus decision stayed within budget + tolerance. It is not restricted to MCTS/PUCT: since #167 A a budgeted heuristic seat is also bounded and therefore also observable. *focus_search_deadline_control is the narrower question 'did the search itself run under a deadline'. A 0 ms budget means no deadline (deterministic by simulation count) and makes every 10 s flag false. Official rule fidelity still requires independent gates.
